title: Dentally Pulse: the AI intelligence layer behind a successful dental workflow
html:
Dentally Pulse brings AI into your everyday practice workflow, helping dental teams reduce repetitive admin and reclaim time for patient care – with clinicians in control of every clinical output.

Your clinical expertise is the most valuable thing in your practice. Every hour that goes into typing up notes, re-entering the same information or chasing an admin task is an hour it isn’t going into directly caring for your patients. Dentally Pulse exists to change that balance. It’s the intelligence layer running behind Dentally, the cloud-based practice management software from Henry Schein One, and it’s built to give clinical time back to the people who need it most.

Why this matters now

Practices are doing more with the same team. Patient expectations have risen, regulation has grown and the working day has filled with tasks that pull clinicians away from the chair. Most of these tasks aren’t complex, they’re just repetitive, and they add up.

Then there’s information entered twice. What a patient tells reception doesn’t always reach the surgery, and what happened in the surgery isn’t always ready at the desk when they leave. Across several surgeries, or several sites, that gap is where time quietly disappears and where attention is taken away from the patient.

Dentally’s guide, Designing a Stress-Free Practice, sets out the effects of this pattern. While individual frustrations like repetitive tasks, missing information and after-hours notes seem minor, together they consume time, drain energy and distract from the reason most people entered the profession in the first place. Almost half of dental professionals expect to leave within the next ten years, with 18% of respondents in the UK citing stress and disillusionment as part of the reason why.

Technology usually answers with more software. Another window, another login, another process to learn. Practices need the opposite: the software they already use, doing more of the heavy lifting.

Pulse is a layer, not a feature

Pulse sits within Dentally rather than alongside it, creating one source of information that can power multiple workflows. Every consultation already holds the information a team will need later. Captured once, it can inform the patient summary, the referral letter and the next appointment plan without anyone having to enter that information again. The work happens once and keeps paying back.

It also means intelligence surfaces where it’s needed rather than where it’s stored: relevant history on the chart as a record opens, or a draft letter ready when a referral is due. Information only creates value when teams can access it at the right moment.

What Pulse does today

Clinical AI notes are live and available now. Rather than typing every detail during or after an appointment, clinicians summarise their findings during the appointment and Dentally generates a structured note for them to review, adjust and save.

It works during the consultation rather than after it, which is what separates it from generic AI tools trying to cover multiple industries with their own specific needs. With Pulse, nobody has to change how they work. The visible result is a shorter catch-up hour at the end of the day, and notes written while the appointment is still fresh rather than three appointments later.

What’s coming next?

Appointment recording is in Beta testing, capturing the appointment as it happens so the record is generated from what was said rather than what’s remembered. Clinical charting is being reimagined around a tooth-first approach, currently in development, so charting follows how clinicians already think rather than how a form is laid out. Smarter booking and communication tools are in discovery, pointing at the next real gain: removing the repetitive front-desk and coordination work that fills a practice manager’s week.

The clinician always has the final say

Pulse is a prompt, not a replacement. It generates the starting point and the clinician decides what happens next. Every output is reviewed and confirmed before it’s saved or sent, and nothing is filed on anyone’s behalf without a person seeing it first.

That isn’t a caveat bolted on as reassurance, it’s the design principle everything else is built on. When a feature carries the Dentally Pulse name, it’s been built with accuracy and designed for real-world dental workflows.

Not AI for the sake of AI.

One intelligent layer

Pulse works as a single connected layer across the practice rather than a separate tool for each role. Information stops sitting in silos. What one team knows, another team has, and the patient’s journey stays continuous even when the people in it change.

Explore Dentally Pulse today.
